greek: Καὶ ποιήσεις θυσιαστήριον ἐκ ξύλων ἀσήπτων, πέντε πήχεων τὸ μῆκος καὶ πέντε πήχεων τὸ εὖρος — τετράγωνον ἔσται τὸ θυσιαστήριον — καὶ τριῶν πήχεων τὸ ὕψος αὐτοῦ.
hint: The altar is to be square, five cubits each way and three high, of wood that does not rot.

notes.text: θυσιαστήριον, an altar, one translation, plain text: from θυσιάζω, to sacrifice, the place of sacrifice.

notes.lemma: τὸ μῆκος … τὸ εὖρος … τὸ ὕψος
notes.text: Accusatives of respect after ποιήσεις, as at 25:10 and 25:23: five cubits in its length.
A clause set into the measurements, the altar square, the Hebrew's rābûaʿ yihyeh.

reading: And [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] altar [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of woods|of woods, of firewood, of timbers, of pieces of wood and posts, of sticks|ξύλον]] [[of not liable to decay|of not liable to decay and corruption, of undigested|ἄσηπτος]], of five [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[the length|the length, the distances, the height and tallness and stature|μῆκος]] and of five [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[the breadth|the breadth and width, the in breadth|εὖρος]] — [[with four equal angles|with four equal angles and rectangular, square, squared, perfect|τετράγωνος]] will be the altar — and of three [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[the height|the height, the top and summit and crown|ὕψος]] of it.

greek: καὶ ποιήσεις τὰ κέρατα ἐπὶ τῶν τεσσάρων γωνιῶν· ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔσται τὰ κέρατα· καὶ καλύψεις αὐτὰ χαλκῷ.
hint: Horns rise from the altar's four corners, of one piece with it, all covered in bronze.

notes.text: κέρας, the horn of an animal, and anything that projects; the chain takes up any projection, which earlier units of the word had dropped.
You will cover them, the horns: the Hebrew has wĕṣippîtā ʾōtô, you shall overlay it, the altar.
χαλκός, copper, then metal in general, then bronze; Middle Liddell says expressly that the word is not brass, and the chain leaves brass out, as earlier units of it had not.

reading: and [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] [[the horns of an animal|the horns of an animal, the horn, the things made of horn, the bows, the horns for blowing, the flutes, the drinking-horns, the horn guards and pipes, the horn points, the arms and branches of a river, the wings of an army and fleet, the any projections, the mountain-peaks|κέρας]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] of the four [[of corners|of corners and angles, of joiner's squares|γωνία]]; [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of it will be [[the horns of an animal|the horns of an animal, the horn, the things made of horn, the bows, the horns for blowing, the flutes, the drinking-horns, the horn guards and pipes, the horn points, the arms and branches of a river, the wings of an army and fleet, the any projections, the mountain-peaks|κέρας]]; and [[you will cover with|you will cover with, you will cover, you will cover and grasp, you will bury, you will cover and conceal, you will cover with dishonour and throw a cloud over, you will put over as a covering|καλύπτω]] them [[to copper|to copper, to metal, to bronze, to anything made of brass and metal, to a copper and caldron and urn, to a brasen mirror, to a copper coin|χαλκός]].

greek: καὶ ποιήσεις στεφάνην τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ καὶ τὸν καλυπτῆρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰς φιάλας αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰς κρεάγρας αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ πυρεῖον αὐτοῦ· καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ποιήσεις χαλκᾶ.
hint: The altar's tools follow: a rim, a cover, bowls, flesh-hooks, a fire-pan, every vessel bronze.

notes.text: στεφάνη, anything that encircles, a rim: the Hebrew has sîrōtāyw lĕdaššĕnô, its pots for removing the ashes.
καλυπτήρ, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's covering, sheath, cover, lid, and in the plural tiles, left to the plural.
φιάλη, a broad, flat vessel or bowl, the commas of the entry's adjectives joined with and.
κρεάγρα, a flesh-hook, one translation, plain text.
πυρεῖον, mostly plural in Middle Liddell, pieces of wood rubbed together for fire; one sense, plain text, in the singular. The Hebrew has maḥtōtāyw, its fire-pans.

reading: and [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] [[anything that encircles|anything that encircles, brim, a diadem and coronal, edge, brow of a hill and edge of a cliff|στεφάνη]] to the altar and [[the covering and sheath|the covering and sheath, the cover, the lid|καλυπτήρ]] of it and [[the broad and flat vessels and bowls|the broad and flat vessels and bowls, the cinerary urns, the broad and flat bowls|φιάλη]] of it and the flesh-hooks of it and the piece of wood of it; and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the vessels|the vessels, the implements of any kind, the furniture and house-gear and utensils and chattels, the accoutrements and equipment, the baggage and luggage, the tackling, the gear, the inanimate objects and things, the bodies and vessels|σκεῦος]] of it [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] [[of copper|of copper, bronze and brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]].

greek: καὶ ποιήσεις αὐτῷ ἐσχάραν ἔργῳ δικτυωτῷ χαλκῆν· καὶ ποιήσεις τῇ ἐσχάρᾳ τέσσαρας δακτυλίους χαλκοῦς ἐπὶ τὰ τέσσαρα κλίτη.
hint: A bronze network grate is made for it, with a bronze ring at each of its four sides.

notes.text: ἐσχάρα, the hearth, a pan of coals, an altar for burnt-offerings; the watch-fires, πυρὸς ἐσχάραι, are a phrase's, set aside.
δικτυωτός, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's made in net-fashion, latticed, trellised, and lattice.
κλίτος, which Middle Liddell gives as κλίμα II, a clime, one translation, plain text, as at 26:18.

reading: and [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] to it [[hearth and fire-place|hearth and fire-place, pan of coals and brasier, altar for burnt-offerings|ἐσχάρα]] [[to work|to work, to business, to deeds, to action, to works of industry and tilled lands|ἔργον]] [[to made in net-fashion|to made in net-fashion, to latticed and trellised, to lattice|δικτυωτός]] [[of copper|of copper, bronze and brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]]; and [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] [[to the hearth and fire-place|to the hearth and fire-place, to the pan of coals and brasier, to the altar for burnt-offerings|ἐσχάρα]] four [[rings|rings and seal-rings|δακτύλιος]] [[of copper|of copper, bronze and brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] the four climes.

greek: καὶ ὑποθήσεις αὐτοὺς ὑπὸ τὴν ἐσχάραν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου κάτωθεν· ἔσται δὲ ἡ ἐσχάρα ἕως τοῦ ἡμίσους τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου.
hint: The rings go beneath the grate, which reaches halfway up the altar.

notes.text: Under the grate: the Hebrew has taḥat karkōb, under the ledge, a word the Greek does not render.
ἥμισυς, the neuter genitive, of the half, after ἕως.

reading: and [[you will place under|you will place under, you will place under one's feet, you will place under as a foundation, you will suggest and advise, you will set before, you will pledge and mortgage|ὑποτίθημι]] them [[towards and under|towards and under, under and into, under and before, under, in subjection, towards, about, about the time, to a certain degree and in some measure|ὑπό + accusative]] [[the hearth and fire-place|the hearth and fire-place, the pan of coals and brasier, the altar for burnt-offerings|ἐσχάρα]] of the altar [[from below|from below and up from below, from the low country and from the coast, below and beneath|κάτωθεν]]; will be [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the hearth and fire-place|the hearth and fire-place, the pan of coals and brasier, the altar for burnt-offerings|ἐσχάρα]] [[until|until, till, while and so long as|ἕως]] [[of the half|of the half, of the half of, of the one half|ἥμισυς]] of the altar.

greek: καὶ ποιήσεις τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ φορεῖς ἐκ ξύλων ἀσήπτων καὶ περιχαλκώσεις αὐτοὺς χαλκῷ.
hint: Carrying poles of the same wood are made for the altar and sheathed in bronze.

notes.text: φορεύς, a bearer, carrier, the poles; the Hebrew has baddîm, poles. Middle Liddell's pack-, of a pack-horse, is a piece of an example, set aside.
περιχαλκόω, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's cover with brass or copper, citing this verse, one translation, plain text.

reading: and [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] to the altar [[bearers|bearers and carriers|φορεύς]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of woods|of woods, of firewood, of timbers, of pieces of wood and posts, of sticks|ξύλον]] [[of not liable to decay|of not liable to decay and corruption, of undigested|ἄσηπτος]] and you will cover with brass or copper them [[to copper|to copper, to metal, to bronze, to anything made of brass and metal, to a copper and caldron and urn, to a brasen mirror, to a copper coin|χαλκός]].

greek: καὶ εἰσάξεις τοὺς φορεῖς εἰς τοὺς δακτυλίους, καὶ ἔστωσαν οἱ φορεῖς κατὰ τὰ πλευρὰ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἐν τῷ αἴρειν αὐτό.
hint: The poles run through the rings along the altar's sides, for lifting it.

notes.text: You will lead in, active, with Moses the subject: the Hebrew has wĕhûbāʾ, shall be brought, passive.
πλευρόν, a rib, the ribs, the side, the neuter, as Middle Liddell files it beside πλευρά.
ἐν with the articular infinitive, in the taking up.

reading: and [[you will lead in|you will lead in, you will lead into and introduce, you will admit, you will import, you will call in, you will bring in and bring forward|εἰσάγω]] [[the bearers|the bearers and carriers|φορεύς]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the rings|the rings and seal-rings|δακτύλιος]], and let be [[the bearers|the bearers and carriers|φορεύς]] [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[the ribs|the ribs, the ribs and the sides, the sides, the flanks|πλευρόν]] of the altar [[in the taking up|within, inside of, and by means of the taking up and raising and lifting up, the bearing and sustaining, the raising up and exalting, the exciting, the extolling and exaggerating, the lifting and taking away and removing, the taking off and killing|ἐν; αἴρω]] it.

greek: κοῖλον σανιδωτὸν ποιήσεις αὐτό· κατὰ τὸ παραδειχθέν σοι ἐν τῷ ὄρει, οὕτως ποιήσεις αὐτό.
hint: The altar is hollow, of planks, made as it was shown on the mountain.

notes.text: κοῖλος, hollow, an adjective here: the chain takes its senses as an adjective, and leaves to the noun the hold, the vale, the valley, a hollow, cavity, ravine, the cavities.
σανιδωτός, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's planked, boarded over, citing this verse.
παραδείκνυμι, the aorist passive participle, the thing exhibited; the middle's to exhibit, bring forward is left out.

reading: [[hollow|hollow and hollowed, lying in a hollow, forming a hollow, lying between high cliffs, embayed, nearly empty|κοῖλος]] [[planked|planked and boarded over|σανιδωτός]] [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] it; [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[the thing having been exhibited side by side|the thing having been exhibited side by side, the thing having been represented, the thing having been exhibited and handed over|παραδείκνυμι]] to you [[in the mountain|within, inside of, and by means of the mountain and hill|ἐν; ὄρος]], [[in this way|in this way, in this manner, so, thus, even so, so much|οὕτως]] [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] it.

greek: Καὶ ποιήσεις αὐλὴν τῇ σκηνῇ· εἰς τὸ κλίτος τὸ πρὸς λίβα ἱστία τῆς αὐλῆς ἐκ βύσσου κεκλωσμένης, μῆκος ἑκατὸν πηχῶν τῷ ἑνὶ κλίτει·
hint: The court begins: on the south-west side, hangings of twisted linen a hundred cubits long.

notes.text: αὐλή, the court-yard, the court or quadrangle, any court or hall.
The article τό, neuter with κλίτος, over the phrase, the thing; λίψ, the SW. wind, one sense, plain text. The Hebrew has negbâ têmānâ, the south side.
ἱστίον, any web, a sail, one translation; Middle Liddell's sail and the sails, from its examples, are repeats, set aside.

reading: And [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] [[court-yard|court-yard, wall of the court-yard, court, quadrangle, any court, hall|αὐλή]] [[to the covered place|to the covered place and tent, to the camp, to the dwelling-place, to the temple|σκηνή]]; [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] the clime the thing [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] SW. wind [[any webs|any webs and sails|ἱστίον]] [[of the court-yard|of the court-yard, of the wall of the court-yard, of the court, of the quadrangle, of the any court, of the hall|αὐλή]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of a fine flax|of a fine flax, of linen made from it|βύσσος]] [[of having been twisted by spinning|of having been twisted by spinning and spun and standing so|κλώθω]], [[length|length, distances, height and tallness and stature|μῆκος]] of a hundred [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[to the one|to the one, to a single one and one alone|εἷς]] to clime;

greek: καὶ οἱ στῦλοι αὐτῶν εἴκοσι, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν εἴκοσι χαλκαῖ, καὶ οἱ κρίκοι αὐτῶν καὶ αἱ ψαλίδες αὐτῶν ἀργυραῖ.
hint: Twenty pillars stand on twenty bronze bases, with silver rings and bands.

notes.text: Of them, the neuter, the hangings.
ψαλίς, a pair of scissors, a vaulted building: the Hebrew has ḥăšuqêhem, their bands.
κρίκος, a ring, for the Hebrew wāwê, hooks.

reading: and [[the pillars|the pillars, the supports and bearings|στῦλος]] of them twenty, and [[the steppings and steps|the steppings and steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps and feet, the those whereon one stands and bases|βάσις]] of them twenty [[of copper|of copper, bronze and brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]], and [[the rings|the rings, the eyelet-holes|κρίκος]] of them and [[the pairs of scissors|the pairs of scissors, the buildings with a pointed stone roof and vaults|ψαλίς]] of them [[silver|silver and of silver|ἀργυροῦς]].

greek: οὕτως τῷ κλίτει τῷ πρὸς ἀπηλιώτην ἱστία, ἑκατὸν πηχῶν μῆκος· καὶ οἱ στῦλοι αὐτῶν εἴκοσι, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν εἴκοσι χαλκαῖ, καὶ οἱ κρίκοι καὶ αἱ ψαλίδες τῶν στύλων καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν περιηργυρωμέναι ἀργύρῳ.
hint: The east side matches it: a hundred cubits, twenty pillars, silver-cased fittings.

notes.text: Toward the east wind: the Hebrew has ṣāpôn, north. ἀπηλιώτης, the wind that comes from the rising sun, the east wind.
περιαργυρόω, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's case, plate with silver, its passive citing this verse; the perfect participle.
ἄργυρος, white metal, silver; Middle Liddell's white is the gloss of ἀργός, from which it derives, set aside.

reading: [[in this way|in this way, in this manner, so, thus, even so, so much|οὕτως]] to the clime to the thing [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[wind that comes from the rising sun|wind that comes from the rising sun and east wind|ἀπηλιώτης]] [[any webs|any webs and sails|ἱστίον]], of a hundred [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[length|length, distances, height and tallness and stature|μῆκος]]; and [[the pillars|the pillars, the supports and bearings|στῦλος]] of them twenty, and [[the steppings and steps|the steppings and steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps and feet, the those whereon one stands and bases|βάσις]] of them twenty [[of copper|of copper, bronze and brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]], and [[the rings|the rings, the eyelet-holes|κρίκος]] and [[the pairs of scissors|the pairs of scissors, the buildings with a pointed stone roof and vaults|ψαλίς]] [[of the pillars|of the pillars, of the supports and bearings|στῦλος]] and [[the steppings and steps|the steppings and steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps and feet, the those whereon one stands and bases|βάσις]] of them [[having been cased|having been cased and plated with silver and standing so|περιαργυρόω]] [[to white metal|to white metal, to silver, to silver-money and money|ἄργυρος]].

greek: τὸ δὲ εὖρος τῆς αὐλῆς τὸ κατὰ θάλασσαν ἱστία πεντήκοντα πηχῶν· στῦλοι αὐτῶν δέκα, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν δέκα.
hint: On the seaward side the court is fifty cubits across, on ten pillars.

notes.text: The article τό, neuter with εὖρος, over the phrase, the thing; toward the sea, the west, as the Hebrew yām.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the breadth|the breadth and width, the in breadth|εὖρος]] [[of the court-yard|of the court-yard, of the wall of the court-yard, of the court, of the quadrangle, of the any court, of the hall|αὐλή]] the thing [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[sea|sea, the Mediterranean, a well of salt water|θάλασσα]] [[any webs|any webs and sails|ἱστίον]] of fifty [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]]; [[pillars|pillars, supports and bearings|στῦλος]] of them ten, and [[the steppings and steps|the steppings and steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps and feet, the those whereon one stands and bases|βάσις]] of them ten.

greek: καὶ εὖρος τῆς αὐλῆς τὸ πρὸς νότον ἱστία πεντήκοντα πήχεων· στῦλοι αὐτῶν δέκα, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν δέκα.
hint: The south side is fifty cubits as well, on ten pillars.

notes.text: Toward the south: the Hebrew has qēdmâ mizrāḥâ, eastward, toward the sunrise.
πῆχυς, printed πήχεων here and πηχῶν at 27:12, the two genitive plurals as the page has them.

reading: and [[breadth|breadth and width, in breadth|εὖρος]] [[of the court-yard|of the court-yard, of the wall of the court-yard, of the court, of the quadrangle, of the any court, of the hall|αὐλή]] the thing [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[south|south and south-west wind, Notus, south and south-west quarter|νότος]] [[any webs|any webs and sails|ἱστίον]] of fifty [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]]; [[pillars|pillars, supports and bearings|στῦλος]] of them ten, and [[the steppings and steps|the steppings and steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps and feet, the those whereon one stands and bases|βάσις]] of them ten.

greek: καὶ πεντεκαίδεκα πήχεων τὸ ὕψος τῶν ἱστίων τῷ κλίτει τῷ ἑνί· στῦλοι αὐτῶν τρεῖς, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν τρεῖς.
hint: One side of the entrance has hangings fifteen cubits high on three pillars.

notes.text: The height: the Hebrew gives fifteen cubits of hangings lakkātēp, for the side, with no height.
πεντεκαίδεκα, fifteen, one word.

reading: and of fifteen [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[the height|the height, the top and summit and crown|ὕψος]] [[of the any webs|of the any webs and sails|ἱστίον]] to the clime [[to the one|to the one, to a single one and one alone|εἷς]]; [[pillars|pillars, supports and bearings|στῦλος]] of them three, and [[the steppings and steps|the steppings and steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps and feet, the those whereon one stands and bases|βάσις]] of them three.

greek: καὶ τὸ κλίτος τὸ δεύτερον, δέκα πέντε πηχῶν τῶν ἱστίων τὸ ὕψος· στῦλοι αὐτῶν τρεῖς, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν τρεῖς.
hint: The other side of the entrance is the same, written 'ten five' cubits, on three pillars.

notes.text: Ten five, two words, where 27:14 has πεντεκαίδεκα, one.
δεύτερος, the neuter with κλίτος; where the chain gives the adjective with the article a noun of its own, the thing.

reading: and the clime [[the second|the second, the thing coming in second, the next best, the next, the thing after, the secondly and next and afterwards and a second time, the second time, the secondary, the second of two|δεύτερος]], of ten of five [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[of the any webs|of the any webs and sails|ἱστίον]] [[the height|the height, the top and summit and crown|ὕψος]]; [[pillars|pillars, supports and bearings|στῦλος]] of them three, and [[the steppings and steps|the steppings and steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps and feet, the those whereon one stands and bases|βάσις]] of them three.

greek: καὶ τῇ πύλῃ τῆς αὐλῆς κάλυμμα, εἴκοσι πηχῶν τὸ ὕψος, ἐξ ὑακίνθου καὶ πορφύρας καὶ κοκκίνου κεκλωσμένου καὶ βύσσου κεκλωσμένης τῇ ποικιλίᾳ τοῦ ῥαφιδευτοῦ· στῦλοι αὐτῶν τέσσαρες, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν τέσσαρες.
hint: The gate of the court has an embroidered covering twenty cubits high, on four pillars.

notes.text: κάλυμμα, a head-covering, hood, veil, covering, for the Hebrew māsāk, screen.
The height again, where the Hebrew gives twenty cubits and no dimension.
ποικιλία, a marking with various colours, embroidery; the plural's pieces of broidery left to the plural.
ῥαφιδευτής, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's stitcher, embroiderer, citing this verse.

reading: and [[to the one wing of a pair of double gates|to the one wing of a pair of double gates, to the gates of a town, to the house-door, to the nether world and hell, to the entrance, to the orifice, to the entrance into a country through mountains and the mountain-pass, to the narrow straits|πύλη]] [[of the court-yard|of the court-yard, of the wall of the court-yard, of the court, of the quadrangle, of the any court, of the hall|αὐλή]] [[a head-covering|a head-covering, a hood, veil, a covering, a grave|κάλυμμα]], of twenty [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[the height|the height, the top and summit and crown|ὕψος]], [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of hyacinth|of hyacinth, of sapphire|ὑάκινθος]] and [[of purple-fish|of purple-fish, of purple dye and purple, of purple raiment|πορφύρα]] and of scarlet [[of having been twisted by spinning|of having been twisted by spinning and spun and standing so|κλώθω]] and [[of a fine flax|of a fine flax, of linen made from it|βύσσος]] [[of having been twisted by spinning|of having been twisted by spinning and spun and standing so|κλώθω]] [[to the marking with various colours|to the marking with various colours and embroidering and embroidery, to the varied aspect and diversity, to the versatility and subtlety and craft|ποικιλία]] [[of the stitcher|of the stitcher and embroiderer|ῥαφιδευτής]]; [[pillars|pillars, supports and bearings|στῦλος]] of them four, and [[the steppings and steps|the steppings and steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps and feet, the those whereon one stands and bases|βάσις]] of them four.

greek: πάντες οἱ στῦλοι τῆς αὐλῆς κύκλῳ κατηργυρωμένοι ἀργυρίῳ, καὶ αἱ κεφαλίδες αὐτῶν ἀργυραῖ, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν χαλκαῖ.
hint: Every pillar round the court is silvered, with silver capitals and bronze bases.

notes.text: καταργυρόω, the perfect passive participle: covered with silver, and the passive's own silvered, and bought or bribed with silver.
κεφαλίς, for the Hebrew wāwêhem, their hooks.

reading: [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the pillars|the pillars, the supports and bearings|στῦλος]] [[of the court-yard|of the court-yard, of the wall of the court-yard, of the court, of the quadrangle, of the any court, of the hall|αὐλή]] [[in a circle|in a circle, in a ring and round about|κύκλῳ]] [[having been covered with silver|having been covered with silver and standing so, having been silvered, having been bought, having been bribed with silver|καταργυρόω]] [[to a piece of silver|to a piece of silver and silver coin, to money and a sum of money and cash, to silver|ἀργύριον]], and [[the parts of a shoe|the parts of a shoe, the heads and chapters|κεφαλίς]] of them [[silver|silver and of silver|ἀργυροῦς]], and [[the steppings and steps|the steppings and steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps and feet, the those whereon one stands and bases|βάσις]] of them [[of copper|of copper, bronze and brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]].

greek: τὸ δὲ μῆκος τῆς αὐλῆς ἑκατὸν ἐφʼ ἑκατόν, καὶ εὖρος πεντήκοντα ἐπὶ πεντήκοντα, καὶ ὕψος πέντε πηχῶν, ἐκ βύσσου κεκλωσμένης, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν χαλκαῖ.
hint: The whole court: a hundred by a hundred, fifty by fifty, five cubits high.

notes.text: A hundred upon a hundred: the Hebrew has mēʾâ bāʾammâ, a hundred by the cubit; its fifty by fifty the Greek keeps.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the length|the length, the distances, the height and tallness and stature|μῆκος]] [[of the court-yard|of the court-yard, of the wall of the court-yard, of the court, of the quadrangle, of the any court, of the hall|αὐλή]] a hundred [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] a hundred, and [[breadth|breadth and width, in breadth|εὖρος]] fifty [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] fifty, and [[height|height, top and summit and crown|ὕψος]] of five [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]], [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of a fine flax|of a fine flax, of linen made from it|βύσσος]] [[of having been twisted by spinning|of having been twisted by spinning and spun and standing so|κλώθω]], and [[the steppings and steps|the steppings and steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps and feet, the those whereon one stands and bases|βάσις]] of them [[of copper|of copper, bronze and brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]].

greek: καὶ πᾶσα ἡ κατασκευὴ καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐργαλεῖα καὶ οἱ πάσσαλοι τῆς αὐλῆς χαλκοῖ.
hint: All the court's fittings, tools and pegs are bronze.

notes.text: κατασκευή, preparation, equipment, fixed furniture; ἐν κατασκευῇ, in preparing for, is a phrase's, set aside.
ἐργαλεῖον, a tool, instrument, one translation run.
πάσσαλος, a peg, a gag.

reading: and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the preparation|the preparation, the equipment, the any kind of furniture that is fixed, the building and fixture, the any furniture, the state and condition and constitution, the device and trick|κατασκευή]] and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the tools|the tools and instruments|ἐργαλεῖον]] and [[the pegs|the pegs, the gags|πάσσαλος]] [[of the court-yard|of the court-yard, of the wall of the court-yard, of the court, of the quadrangle, of the any court, of the hall|αὐλή]] [[of copper|of copper, bronze and brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]].

greek: Καὶ σὺ σύνταξον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ισραηλ καὶ λαβέτωσάν σοι ἔλαιον ἐξ ἐλαίων ἄτρυγον καθαρὸν κεκομμένον εἰς φῶς καῦσαι, ἵνα κάηται λύχνος διὰ παντός.
hint: Israel is to bring pure beaten olive oil, so that a lamp burns continually.

notes.text: ἔλαιον, olive-oil, its genitive plural by the accent: ἐλαία's, the olive, would be ἐλαιῶν. Oil out of oils.
ἄτρυγος, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's without lees, clarified, pure, citing this verse.
καθαρός, clear of dirt, clean; the chain takes up clear of guilt, purified, without blemish and clear, exact, which earlier units of the word had dropped.

κόπτω, the perfect passive participle, struck, beaten; the middle's senses, to beat one's breast, to mourn for, are left out. Where the active's English has its object inside a phrase, κ. τὴν χώραν to cut down the trees in it, to lay it waste, the passive is said in English's own way, the land the subject: having had the trees in it cut down, having been laid waste.
Through all, παντός neuter, continually, as at 25:30.

reading: And you [[put in order together|put in order together, draw up and put in array, arrange and organise, concoct, fix and assess, ordain and prescribe|συντάσσω]] to the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] and [[let them take|let them take, let them receive, let them take hold of and grasp and seize|λαμβάνω]] to you olive-oil [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of olive-oils [[without lees|without lees and clarified and pure|ἄτρυγος]] [[clear of dirt|clear of dirt and clean and spotless and unsoiled, clear and open and free, clear from shame and pollution and pure, clear of guilt and defilement and clean and pure, purified, clear of and from, clear of admixture and clear and pure, pure and genuine, without blemish, clear and exact|καθαρός]] [[having been struck|having been struck and smitten and knocked down and standing so, having been cut off and chopped off, having been felled, having had the trees in it cut down, having been laid waste, having been shattered, having been disabled, stricken, having been hammered and forged, having been stamped, having been coined, having been knocked at, having been cut small and chopped up, having been pounded, having been jolted, having been shaken, having been tired out and wearied|κόπτω]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[light|light and daylight, a light, eyes|φάος]] [[to light|to light and kindle, to set on fire and burn up and burn, to burn and scorch, to burn and destroy, to cauterise|καίω]], [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] [[may be lighted|may be lighted and kindled, may be lighted and burn, may be set on fire and burned up and burned, may be burned and scorched, may be burnt, may be parched up, may be burned and destroyed, may be cauterised|καίω]] [[a portable light|a portable light and lamp|λύχνος]] [[through|through, right through, by means of, by the agency of|διά + genitive]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single|πᾶς]].

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of Genesis 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")

greek: ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἔξωθεν τοῦ καταπετάσματος τοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς διαθήκης καύσει αὐτὸ Ααρων καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ ἀφʼ ἑσπέρας ἕως πρωὶ ἐναντίον κυρίου· νόμιμον αἰώνιον εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ.
hint: Aaron and his sons tend the lamp from evening to morning, a statute for all generations.

notes.text: Will light: the Hebrew has yaʿărōk, shall set in order.
Of the covenant, διαθήκη, where the Hebrew has hāʿēdut, the testimony.
The article τοῦ, neuter with καταπέτασμα, over the phrase, of the thing.
Of you: the Hebrew has lĕdōrōtām, their generations.

reading: [[in the covered place|within, inside of, and by means of the covered place and tent, the camp, the dwelling-place, the temple|ἐν; σκηνή]] [[of the testimony|of the testimony and proof|μαρτύριον]] [[from without|from without, outside, without and free from|ἔξωθεν]] [[of the curtain|of the curtain and veil|καταπέτασμα]] of the thing [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the disposition|of the disposition of property by will, of the will and testament, of the arrangement between two parties, of the covenant|διαθήκη]] [[will light|will light and kindle, will set on fire and burn up and burn, will burn and scorch, will burn and destroy, will cauterise|καίω]] it [[name:Ααρων]] and the sons of him [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of evening|of evening, of eventide, of eve, of nightfall, of the west|ἑσπέρα]] [[until|until, till, while and so long as|ἕως]] [[early in the day|early in the day, early, at morn, betimes, in good time, too soon and too early|πρωΐ]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of and before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] [[of lord|of lord / master, of the head, of master, of the Lord, of Jehovah|κύριος]]; [[usage|usage and custom, funeral rites|νόμιμος]] [[lasting for an age|lasting for an age, ever-lasting and eternal|αἰώνιος]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the races|the races and stocks and families, the breeds, the tribes and nations, the races and generations, the offspring, the birth-places, the ages and times of life, the times of birth|γενεά]] of you [[from the side of|from the side of, from beside, from, near|παρά + genitive]] of the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]].
